title: A JSON parser
hints: `value()` looks at the next non-space character to decide: `{` object, `[` array, `"` string, `t`/`f`/`n` a literal, otherwise a number (lesson 8.05).
Keep the line and column up to date as you take each character, so every error can use them.

For a `\u` escape, read the next four characters into a `String`, turn them into a number with `u32::from_str_radix(&hex, 16)` (lesson 8.02), and then into a character with `char::from_u32(n)`, which returns `None` for numbers that are not valid characters.
requirements: `enum Json { Null, Bool(bool), Number(f64), String(String), Array(Vec<Json>), Object(Vec<(String, Json)>) }`.
A recursive-descent parser over the characters, with string escapes (`\"`, `\\`, `\n`, and `é` for `é`).
Errors with the line and column; `Display` for `Json` that writes valid JSON back.
stretch: Compare your output with `serde_json` on a few files, and measure the speed.
